title: Story Backlog
description: Output of story-converter in spec mode, produced once per project by project-planner. Written to .claude/state/story-backlog.json as a single JSON object matching this schema exactly - not JSON Lines, since the backlog is written once (or once per re-run against an already-planned project), never appended to incrementally. A point-in-time snapshot of what spec mode produced: story-converter's plan mode never rewrites it, only the ticket system reflects changes after creation. Each story is later handed off to an independent feature-orchestrator run.

program_spec_ref.description: Path or reference to the approved program-level spec this backlog was generated from.

architecture_mode.description: Set once by project-planner when architecture mode was explicitly requested at invocation. Persists past that single run so story-converter's context_mode defaulting, a later project-planner re-run, or a human can see it without re-deriving anything. When true, grill-me and spec-writer were told to go deep on service boundaries/data ownership/integration patterns during planning rather than deferring that detail per-story, and story-converter should weigh it toward more stories defaulting to full-spec context_mode.

ticket_id.description: The one ticket story-converter created for this story in spec mode. feature-orchestrator's amendment loops and completion sync (plan mode) always update this same ticket — nothing downstream creates a second one.

context_mode.description: full-spec: story's feature-orchestrator run loads the whole program spec. decision-log-only: loads just the shared decision log. independent: loads neither. In every mode, this story's own decision-recorder writes still happen unconditionally.

depends_on.description: Other story ids this one has a genuine contract dependency on — e.g. this story consumes an API, schema, or interface another story builds, and literally cannot be correctly implemented without knowing its shape. This is the only reason to set depends_on. A story that merely might benefit from knowing a decision another story is likely to make is not a dependency — that's what context escalation (see feature-orchestrator) is for, and it doesn't block anything. Sequencing 5 of 10 stories on contract dependencies alone should be rare; sequencing them because of a decision one might want to be aware of would defeat the point of running stories in parallel at all.
